insights.title: Early-phase trials are a much longer trip
insights.headline: 85.8 million
insights.headline_label: residents beyond 25 mi of a recruiting Phase 1 site
insights.text: Phase 1 studies are where new drugs first reach patients. Only 74.1% of residents live within 25 miles of a site recruiting for one, against 90.9% for any oncology trial: 55.6 million more people are out of range. The median resident is 8.5 miles from an early-phase site versus 4.0 miles from any site.

insights.title: Some 'recruiting' records have not been checked in over a year
insights.headline_label: of recruiting oncology studies not status-verified in the last 12 months
insights.text: 624 of 6,928 studies listed as Recruiting were last verified by their sponsor more than 12 months before this registry release (142 more than two years before). Counting only recently verified studies moves 737,055 residents outside 25 miles. TrialGraph keeps both views so planners can see how much a stale record could flatter a region.

insights.title: Where distance and economic barriers stack up
insights.headline_label: counties are both an access gap and in the top quartile for poverty or uninsurance
insights.text: These 743 counties are home to 15.5 million people. Most of their residents live more than 25 miles from a recruiting site, and they rank in the highest-need quarter of U.S. counties for poverty or lack of insurance (ACS). The largest are Okaloosa County, FL, Yuma County, AZ, Imperial County, CA.

insights.title: Upper age limits quietly shrink access for older adults
insights.headline_label: of recruiting interventional studies exclude people aged 75+
insights.text: 511 of 5,679 recruiting interventional oncology studies set a maximum age below 75, even though cancer incidence peaks in older adults. Restricted to studies open to people 75 and over, 90.6% of residents are within 25 miles (1.1 million fewer than for all studies). This uses registry age limits only - real eligibility criteria are stricter.

insights.title: Texas has the most rural residents out of range
insights.headline: 2.3 million
insights.text: Ranked by the number of non-metro residents farther than the threshold from a recruiting site: Texas 2.3 million (19% within); Oklahoma 1.1 million (16% within); Alabama 999,399 (11% within); Arkansas 933,960 (22% within); Georgia 929,161 (48% within).

insights.title: Trial activity is concentrated in a few hubs
insights.headline_label: of recruiting study-site slots are at the busiest 5% of sites
insights.text: 14,179 facility records host a recruiting interventional oncology study, but the busiest 709 account for 50% of all recruiting study-site listings. Only 905 of 3,144 counties contain any recruiting site; they hold 82% of the population.

insights.title: Liver & biliary trials are the hardest to reach
insights.headline: 115.8 million
insights.headline_label: residents beyond 25 mi of a recruiting liver & biliary site
insights.text: Coverage varies sharply by cancer type: 87.0% of residents are within 25 miles of a recruiting breast site, but only 65.1% for liver & biliary. Planning on the all-oncology map hides these gaps.

insights.title: New sites alone cannot close the gap
insights.headline_label: of the 25-mile gap closed by 10 well-placed hypothetical sites
insights.text: Placing hypothetical sites one at a time purely for coverage, the first three (Montgomery County, TN, Etowah County, AL, Okaloosa County, FL) would bring 807,433 of the 30.2 million out-of-range residents within 25 miles (3%); 10 sites reach 7%. Even the best-placed site adds only 1% because the remaining gap is spread across many small, remote communities. That pattern suggests decentralised or remote-participation models may matter more than additional brick-and-mortar sites for the last stretch.
